title: Sign in
what: Email and password. A temporary password forces a change on first sign-in; 'remember me' keeps the session on this browser. Five wrong passwords in 15 minutes pauses the account.
bullets: Reset link goes to e-mail (demo build: printed in the API log)
Theme switch (light/dark) top right
Account menu after sign-in: change password, sign out

title: Organizations
what: The customer's legal entities. Everything else in the engagement hangs off one of these.
bullets: Create organization: legal name and basics
Table lists what exists; open a row to edit
Deleting is a soft close, history stays

title: Tenants
what: The Microsoft 365 / Azure tenants in scope (GCC or GCC High). In the demo the tenant points at the simulator.
bullets: Register tenant: name, cloud, identifiers
Connection checks show whether the platform can reach it
No credentials are stored here — the runner holds the certificate

title: Scope — CUI boundary
role: compliance manager drafts · org admin confirms
what: Which systems and assets handle CUI. Confirming a boundary version is a formal act: it is what the assessor sees as 'what you said was in scope'.
bullets: Assets by category: CUI, SPA, CRMA, Specialized, Out of scope
Draft → Confirm (org admin only); every version kept
Narrative and data flows attached to the boundary

title: Systems inventory
what: The systems and environments registry: name, environment, owner. Feeds the SSP system description later.
bullets: Add a system with its environment and owner
Everyone reads; compliance manager and org admin edit

title: Onboarding checklist
what: What is done and what is still missing before an assessment makes sense. No actions here — it tells you where to go.
bullets: Organization, tenant, boundary, systems, first run
Each item links to the page that completes it

title: Readiness assessment
role: compliance manager · IT security admin · BHD operator
what: The main screen. Pick the engagement and a run; the family table shows met / partial / not met / unknown per control family and the SPRS score. Run assessment reads the tenant (simulator or live) — never writes.
bullets: Run assessment: 'Engine running…' on Windows, 'Queued…' until a runner picks it up elsewhere
Unknown is honest: ~150 of 320 objectives need a document or a person
Import readiness result: load a result file produced elsewhere (BHD)

title: Gap analysis
what: Every requirement that is not met or unknown, heaviest first (SPRS weights 1/3/5). Open a gap for its objectives; Override sets a status by hand with a reason, recorded under your name.
bullets: Export CSV for the working session with the customer
Override needs a reason of at least ten characters and is audited
Fixable gaps point at Stamper registry entries

title: Planning overview
what: Counts by priority and status across actions and POA&M items.
bullets: Open vs in progress vs done
Which gaps have no action yet

title: Action items
what: One row per thing to do: requirement, owner, priority, due date, fix kind. 'Registry' fix kind means Stamper can do it automatically.
bullets: Generate from gaps, or add by hand
open → in progress → done / won't fix
Export CSV

title: POA&M
role: compliance manager edits · senior approver approves
what: The Plan of Action & Milestones an assessor expects: weakness, mitigation, milestones with dates, and whether a POA&M is even allowed for that requirement.
bullets: Build from actions in one click
Rows marked NO cannot be deferred — they must be met

title: Remediation overview
what: Every run across both engines: who requested, module, mode (simulate / live), cost, gates, status. Open a run for its drawer: gates, result, and the actions your role has.
bullets: Awaiting approval → Approved → (Queued → Running) → Finished · verify → Verified
Rejected, Blocked by gate, Cancelled are terminal
Simulate never touches the tenant

title: Stamper — configuration management
what: Configuration changes from BHD's registry. Pick entries (get = read-only check, set = changes something, HELD = manual), choose simulate or live, justify, request.
bullets: A get-only run is approved on request; any set entry needs a second BHD operator (DP-2)
Live needs the engagement's live-access flag and consent, re-checked at every hop
Execute records the plan (simulate) or queues it for the Windows runner (live)

title: AdminOps — governed admin operations
role: IT security admin requests · senior approver or BHD approves
what: Day-2 admin operations by domain (Identity & Access, Devices, Credentials, Data Protection, Audit…). Pick an operation, fill its parameters, justify, request.
bullets: Parameters never hold secrets — the platform refuses them (PB-02)
Same approval and execute flow as Stamper
Other customer roles see the queue, cannot request

title: Evidence overview
what: Counts by status (draft, submitted, validated, rejected) and by source (discovery, stamper, adminops, manual).
bullets: Coverage: which requirements have evidence, which do not
Evidence requests outstanding

title: Evidence explorer
what: Every item: title, requirement(s), objective(s), source, SHA-256, size, status. Open one for the content preview, who created and reviewed it, and the run it came from.
bullets: Lists never load content — open the item
Captures from assessment runs arrive here as drafts automatically

title: Collect evidence
role: compliance manager · IT security admin · BHD operator
what: Upload a file or paste text; choose requirement and objectives; optionally pick a catalog definition — what the assessor expects for that requirement. Submit for review.
bullets: Inline evidence up to 10 MB; hash computed on save
Pre-set definition from the catalog page lands here

title: NIST evidence catalog
what: Per requirement, the NIST 800-171A examine items and the evidence definitions (form ids, what to collect, which objectives it satisfies). Release 0 covers AC.L2-3.1.1; BHD delivers the rest in batches.
bullets: Click a definition → pre-filled Collect form
Batch validator checks new releases before they are vendored

title: Review (as evidence reviewer)
what: The same explorer seen by the reviewer: submitted items can be approved or rejected with a note. You cannot review what you submitted yourself — the page says so.
bullets: Separation of duties enforced by the API, hinted by the UI
New version supersedes, keeps the chain

title: Monitoring overview
role: IT security admin runs · everyone reads
what: Compliance posture over time: findings open / acknowledged / resolved, last evaluation, drift since the last assessment. Evaluate now re-reads what it can; the scheduler does it on the engagement's cadence when switched on.
bullets: Snapshots per evaluation
Drift = requirements that were met and no longer are

title: Alerts
role: anyone with edit acknowledges · senior approver resolves / escalates
what: Findings by family and status. Open one to acknowledge with notes, resolve, or escalate.
bullets: open → acknowledged → resolved; escalated from either
Every change lands in Activity

title: Audit & activity
what: The audit trail for this engagement: who did what, when, filterable by text. This is the answer to 'who changed that'.
bullets: Actor, action, target, time
Approvals, executions, claims, results, overrides all appear here

title: Assessment readiness
what: The checklist for the package: boundary confirmed, assessment run exists, POA&M present, evidence coverage, SSP statements, sign-offs.
bullets: Each line says what is missing and where to fix it

title: System Security Plan (SSP)
what: One row per requirement: implementation statement (draft → approved), implementation status, linked evidence. Generate drafts from the assessment and evidence; export as Markdown.
bullets: Status: implemented · partially · planned · alternative · not applicable
Approving a statement is a separate, audited click

title: Evidence packages
role: compliance manager builds and signs (not the same person)
what: Build an evidence package for a scope (all, a family, a requirement list): Build → Validate → Sign off. Versions are kept; a signed package is immutable.
bullets: The builder cannot sign their own package
Export the manifest for the assessor

title: Assessor workspace (read-only)
what: What the C3PAO assessor sees: the package, read-only, and a request list. They ask for an item; the compliance manager answers with evidence or a note.
bullets: Nothing in this view can change the engagement
Requests: open → answered → closed

title: Reports & exports
what: Readiness, coverage, gaps, SPRS, POA&M and evidence inventory as JSON, Markdown or CSV.
bullets: CSV cells are formula-safe
Same numbers as the screens — one calculator

title: Settings
what: Engagement details (name, reference, CMMC level, status, dates), monitoring cadence, notification settings, and the Modules tab: hide lifecycle sections for everyone in this organisation — a phased roll-out or a demo. Hidden is not disallowed; the API keeps enforcing the role matrix.
bullets: Some settings are recorded but not yet enforced — the tab says which (open with BHD)
Modules: Administration cannot be hidden; takes effect at the next sign-in or reload
Every save is versioned and audited

title: Access management
what: Requests (anyone asks for a role, org admin decides), periodic access reviews (completion attested by a different admin), and Users: org-scoped user admin with customer roles only.
bullets: Never grants platform or BHD roles
Temporary password shown once; last org admin cannot be removed

title: System health
what: Database, integrations (simulator / Graph reachability), the scheduler (on/off, last tick), and when a runner last claimed work. If Run assessment sits in Queued…, look here.
bullets: Platform admin is fenced from tenant health (PB-01) — decision pending with BHD

title: Settings — Modules (show / hide sections)
what: Untick a lifecycle section to hide it from every role in this organisation — for a demo, or to switch sections on as the engagement progresses. Save, then sign in again (or reload) to see the sidebar change.
bullets: Hidden ≠ disallowed: the API still enforces the role matrix
Administration and Shared Foundation cannot be hidden
Audited like every settings change; the BHD operator sees it in Activity
